Scenario.Name: Little Largo Blue Space
Scenario.Author: EcoKnow
Scenario.Description: Over centuries the waters of Largo Bay have been utilised as a resource (whether for commerce or recreation) yet have been gradually contaminated by industry and agriculture on the land. Today agricultural runoff is compounded by sewage and the significant problem of litter, regarded by the community as ‘a hazard’, and the plastics and polystyrene that wash up on the beach is much worse after a storm. The Lower Largo community hope the wastewater treatment facility will mean they ‘meet bathing water quality standards completely’, ensuring the water of Largo Bay would not ‘potentially make [them] seriously ill’. As well as the benefit to the human community, there is a strong desire to ensure a healthy environment for the non-human visitors to these waters: oysters, seals, and seagrass.

WinConditions.Title: Water Pollution Under Control
WinConditions.Description: Bring catchment-wide water pollution down to LOW by the final round. Treatment is the only structural lever once late-round additions ramp up.

WinConditions.Title: Don't Overfish
WinConditions.Description: Leave at least 230 oysters in the bay by the final round. Light-to-moderate foraging (up to ~5 cycles) is sustainable — greedy foraging crashes the bay.

LoseConditions.Title: Dirty-Water Sickness
LoseConditions.Description: Eating oysters from polluted water makes people sick. Three sicknesses ends the game — always check the aggregate tier before foraging.
